title: Non-stationary longitudinal Josephson effect in electron-hole bilayers
authors: O. M. Konstantynov, S. I. Shevchenko
abstract: The non-stationary longitudinal Josephson effect in bilayer systems with pairing of spatially separated electrons and holes is investigated. The tunneling current between two (right and left) weakly coupled electron-hole condensates is analyzed in the presence of an external voltage applied along the layers. Two limiting regimes are considered: the high-density regime, where pairing occurs in momentum space similarly to conventional superconductors, and the low-density regime corresponding to a Bose-Einstein condensate of spatially indirect excitons. Using the tunneling Hamiltonian approach, expressions for the quasiparticle, superconducting and interference contributions to the tunneling current are derived. It is shown that in the high-density limit the quasiparticle and interference currents vanish at zero temperature below a threshold voltage determined by the energy gap, so that only the supercurrent remains. In contrast, in the low-density regime the gapless spectrum of collective excitations leads to finite dissipative contributions even at zero temperature, resulting in damping of Josephson oscillations. For spatially separated tunneling barriers with distance exceeding the coherence length, phase jumps occur at each barrier, resulting in voltage oscillations across the electron and hole barriers and a non-sinusoidal current-phase relation governed by the critical currents of the two barriers.
summary: This theoretical work examines the Josephson effect in electron-hole bilayers, modeling tunneling currents under an external voltage. By analyzing high-density versus low-density regimes, it reveals fundamental differences in current behavior, particularly the emergence of dissipative damping in the excitonic (low-density) limit. The methodology combines advanced many-body techniques with condensed matter physics principles.
main_problem: The study investigates the non-stationary longitudinal Josephson effect occurring in electron-hole bilayers where pairing occurs between spatially separated electrons and holes.
main_result: The system exhibits distinct behaviors depending on carrier density: high-density limits show only supercurrent below a threshold voltage, while low-density regimes feature finite dissipative currents even at zero temperature due to gapless excitations.
method: The analysis employs the tunneling Hamiltonian approach combined with Green's function techniques and perturbation theory to calculate various current components (quasiparticle, superconducting, interference).
model_or_system: The model is an electron-hole bilayer system weakly coupled by a tunnel junction. It is analyzed in two limits: high-density (momentum space pairing) and low-density (Bose-Einstein condensate of excitons).
key_observables: Tunneling current ($I_t$), quasiparticle current ($qI$), supercurrent components, and the relative phase difference ($\varphi_{eh}$).
important_parameters: External applied voltage ($V_t$), carrier density (determining high vs. low-density regime), and energy gap ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbation theory for weak tunneling, treating the system in both BCS-like (high-density) and bosonic/coherent state (low-density) approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the bilayer structure with weak coupling; Figure 2 likely shows phase evolution or current characteristics related to Josephson dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by setting up the Hamiltonian, deriving current expressions using Green's functions in various limits (high/low density), and finally analyzing the resulting dynamical equations for the superconducting phase difference under applied voltage.
why_interesting: It connects concepts from superconductivity (Josephson effect) with quantum gas physics (exciton BEC), providing a rich platform to study non-equilibrium dynamics, dissipation, and phase coherence in artificial quantum systems.
